skill.name: ab-test-setup
skill.description: Guides teams through disciplined A/B test planning with locked hypotheses, metrics, sample-size checks, and execution readiness gates.
skill.summary: Set up rigorous A/B tests with locked hypotheses, clear metrics, sample-size checks, and launch readiness gates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The flagged lines are false positives caused by ordinary A/B testing governance terms such as blocks, valid hypothesis, single metric, and shared searchable records. No evidence found of system reconnaissance, network reconnaissance, prompt injection, code execution, or data exfiltration in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: Store records in a shared, searchable location to avoid repeated failures.
- Single metric used to evaluate success

finding_verdicts.reason: The text says the process blocks invalid hypotheses in an A/B testing checklist. It does not ask the agent to inspect hosts, users, files, or system configuration.
This line introduces criteria for a valid experimentation hypothesis. It is not a command to enumerate a system or collect environment data.
The line tells the user to choose the simplest valid experiment design. No operating system, network, or infrastructure reconnaissance is requested.
The line advises storing test records in a shared searchable location for documentation. It does not request discovery of hosts, files, services, or credentials.
The line defines a single primary metric tied to the hypothesis. It does not scan networks, enumerate services, or make network requests.

content.value_statement: Teams often launch experiments without locked hypotheses, metrics, or sample-size checks. This skill guides A/B test setup with gates for validity and readiness.
actual_capabilities: Guides hypothesis definition before test design begins.
Requires primary, secondary, and guardrail metric selection.
Checks assumptions about traffic, randomization, and external factors.
Helps choose between A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, and split URL tests.
Requires sample size, duration, and execution readiness before launch.
Provides result interpretation and documentation rules.
limitations: Does not calculate exact statistical power without user-provided baseline, MDE, and traffic data.
Does not connect to analytics tools or experimentation platforms.
Does not replace review by a data scientist for high-impact experiments.
Does not automate implementation, tracking, or rollout decisions.

use_cases.title: Lock Experiment Requirements
use_cases.description: Define the hypothesis, target audience, primary metric, and expected effect before design work starts.

use_cases.title: Plan Campaign Tests
use_cases.description: Check that traffic, duration, and guardrail metrics support a valid marketing experiment.

use_cases.title: Review Test Readiness
use_cases.description: Audit an experiment plan for missing assumptions, weak metrics, or launch blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up an A/B test for [product area]. My user problem is [problem]. My proposed change is [change]. Ask for missing hypothesis, audience, metric, baseline, MDE, and traffic details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup from an experiment idea.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this A/B test hypothesis: [hypothesis]. Check for evidence, one specific change, defined audience, expected direction, and measurable success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this A/B test plan for launch readiness: [plan]. Verify locked hypothesis, frozen primary metric, sample size, duration, guardrails, tracking, and weak assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Completed Experiment Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this complete experiment plan and result interpretation: [details]. Identify validity risks, peeking issues, guardrail failures, unsupported causality claims, and missing documentation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced governance review for high-impact tests.

output_examples.input: I want to test a new onboarding checklist for trial users.
output_examples.output: The skill would ask for final hypothesis confirmation, audience, primary metric, expected direction, MDE, baseline rate, and traffic estimate before selecting a test type.

output_examples.input: Our test shows a positive conversion lift but a support ticket increase.
output: Guardrail failure should be reviewed before rollout.
The primary metric win should not override material harm.
Document the result and decide whether to redesign the variant.

output_examples.input: We want to change headline, pricing display, and checkout copy in one test.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag multiple variables and recommend a simpler design, A/B/n planning, or multivariate testing only if traffic supports it.

best_practices: Lock the hypothesis, audience, primary metric, and MDE before creating variants.
Estimate sample size and duration before launch, then avoid early stopping for attractive interim results.
Record decisions, assumptions, external factors, and learnings in a shared experiment log.
anti_patterns: Running several variant changes while treating the result as one simple A/B test.
Shipping a variant that wins the primary metric while failing guardrail metrics.

faq.question: Does this skill run statistical calculations?
faq.answer: It guides required inputs and readiness checks, but exact calculations depend on data the user provides.

faq.question: Can it choose the best test type?
faq.answer: It recommends the simplest valid design based on the number and type of changes.

faq.question: Does it connect to analytics platforms?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the user can provide metric data, traffic estimates, and tracking status.

faq.question: Can it help after a test ends?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides interpretation rules, guardrail checks, and documentation guidance for decisions.

faq.question: Is it only for product teams?
faq.answer: No. Growth, marketing, data, and UX teams can use it for controlled experiments.

faq.question: What information should I prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare the user problem, proposed change, audience, baseline metric, traffic estimate, MDE, and guardrail concerns.
